newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand starts buying from 1996/97 coffee crop.
newsitem.headline: Thailand starts buying from 1996/97 coffee crop.

text.p: The Thai commerce ministry on Wednesday started buying some of the 32,000 tonnes of coffee it plans to export from the 1996/1997 coffee crop (October-November), a ministry source said.

The purchase is a part of a price intervention scheme following a drop in world prices over the past year in which the ministry buys coffee beans from farmers at a guaranteed price of 30 baht ($1.20) a kg.
Total output for this crop year is expected to drop to 62,000 tonnes from around 81,398 tonnes forecast earlier because of rains.
Thailand exported 60,000 tonnes of coffee beans during the 1995/96 crop year from total production of 78,801 tonnes.
The exportable amount this year is expected to drop to 32,000 tonnes due to strong domestic demand which is forecast at 30,000 tonnes.
